outcome: Several genuine cases of the Tate conjecture were settled since January 2024 (abelian fourfolds and, building on that, abelian fivefolds over finite fields; a near-completion for surfaces of geometric genus one), and a stronger integral variant was shown to fail in general — but the conjecture in full generality remains open, and the most sweeping recent claim (a 'full proof' on Zenodo) is an unreviewed, non-expert preprint with no credible standing. No AI system produced or materially contributed to any of the real mathematics found; one AI-oriented research-mapping site (ProofAtlas) has organized the problem into subtasks for human/AI contributors but has not itself produced a result.
summary: The problem as stated (Tate's general conjecture relating algebraic cycles to Galois-invariant classes in étale cohomology) remains open in full generality, so no single decisive event settles it; several genuine cases were settled and I treat the most significant, Broe's proof for abelian fourfolds over finite fields (arXiv:2608.28651, posted 19 Aug 2026), as the anchoring event because it is described as 'the first resolution of the conjecture for all abelian varieties of a fixed dimension over finite fields since Tate's own 1960s work' — a genuine restriction of the stated question (a case, not a variant, per §3.1) that also let Broe complete the standard conjectures for abelian fourfolds. This is a preprint that has already reached seminar discussion (a University of Michigan algebraic-geometry preprint seminar covered it), but as of this research it has not yet been digested by a published expert verification or accepted by a journal, so status is 'claimed' rather than 'resolved'. Within a month, Ningyi Li built on it to prove the Tate conjecture for abelian fivefolds over finite fields (arXiv:2609.06265, Sept 2026), explicitly citing Broe's Theorem 1.1 in a revision — a further case, also 'claimed'. Separately, Guo–Yang's paper on surfaces of geometric genus one (arXiv:2501.18541, posted 30 Jan 2025 — four days inside the window) 'largely completes' the Kuga–Satake program for that case, another genuine case-restriction; and Milne's 2-page note (arXiv:2509.06707, Sept 2025) shows the stronger 'integral' Tate conjecture fails for very general abelian varieties, using a transfer from a recent integral Hodge conjecture counterexample result — this is progress/refutation of a related-but-distinct (stronger) variant, not the base conjecture, so it does not by itself move the base conjecture's status but is noted as context. None of these four genuine results mentions any AI system, machine-learning tool, or automated proof assistant in producing the mathematics; all are traditional human proofs building on named prior results (Ancona, Markman, Kuga–Satake, Deligne). Separately, a September 2025 Zenodo item ('A Constructive Spectral Proof of the Tate Conjecture for Smooth Projective Varieties over Finite Fields', Luis Morató de Dalmases) claims a full, general proof via a self-adjoint 'spectral operator' construction; the same author has simultaneously posted dozens of similarly-titled 'constructive spectral proofs' of the Riemann Hypothesis, Hodge conjecture, P≠NP, Goldbach, BSD, and unrelated physics 'theories of everything' on Zenodo, an unreviewed self-publishing repository — a clear crank-output pattern with no journal, no citations, and no expert digestion found. I do not credit it as changing the conjecture's status, consistent with the triage's own flag of it as 'unverified/unconventional venue'. I also found ProofAtlas, a platform that has built a structured 'research map' of the Tate conjecture inviting human and AI contributors to work on specific open 'gates' — this is infrastructure for future work, not a result, and does not itself change status or count as an AI contribution.
competing_reading: One could argue the correct status is 'partial' rather than 'claimed', since multiple genuine partial cases (fourfolds, fivefolds, genus-one surfaces) are individually well short of full resolution and none is the 'main claim' the way a would-be full proof is; under that reading the Zenodo item is irrelevant noise and the anchoring event should instead be Guo–Yang (Jan 2025) as the most clearly scoped case-restriction with a real application (BSD for certain elliptic curves), still unreviewed by a journal but with no seminar/attention gap. I chose Broe's result as the anchor because it is the most structurally significant restriction (a full dimension, not just a subclass) and has visible expert engagement (the Michigan seminar), but the case for anchoring on Guo–Yang or simply calling the overall status 'partial' (multiple cases moved, nothing resolved) is reasonable.
what_would_settle_it: A published, peer-reviewed version of Broe's or Li's paper, or an expert blog/digest (e.g., Tao, the Stacks Project community, or a MathOverflow consensus) explicitly endorsing the fourfold or fivefold proof, would move that specific case from 'claimed' to 'resolved'. For the overall conjecture, only a proof (or disproof) covering arbitrary codimension on arbitrary smooth projective varieties would settle it — nothing found approaches that except the non-credible Zenodo claim.

corrections.why: SCOPE: `claimed` counted the Tate conjecture among resolutions and the site labelled it 'Proved (claimed)'. The record's own summary says it 'remains open in full generality' and that the anchoring event, Broe's proof for abelian fourfolds over finite fields, is 'a genuine restriction of the stated question (a case, not a variant)'; its competing_reading argues for `partial`. A case settled is `partial` under 6.1. The research rules fold 'how much was settled' and 'has an expert checked it' into one field, and the agent read an unreviewed case as `claimed`; that is the pattern this batch of corrections fixes. The Zenodo 'full proof' the record dismisses as non-expert stays set aside.
